docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (the docs must match the code). (a) The tools table (lines 103-113) predates v0.2. whatif_start also takes business, template and lang. whatif_what_changed, whatif_rehearsal_start, whatif_plan_test and whatif_log_result take 'state' in place of template plus inputs (stateInsteadArg in src/mcp/tools.ts), plus business, question, demo and currency. rehearsal_start also takes customer_mix. whatif_run_scenarios has inputs optional with demo. (b) Line 7 says 'stateless, no auth for now', which contradicts the invite codes. (c) Layout line 31 places the server instructions in tools.ts. They are in src/mcp/instructions.ts, and the layout leaves out src/mcp/messages.ts and src/i18n/. (d) ShareState (line 79) leaves out madeBy and rehearsal.customerMix (src/state.ts:24, :33). (e) The input caps in STATE_LIMITS (src/state.ts:76) are documented nowhere, although limits is a judging criterion. (f) The /try order (line 159) leaves out the first screen, the template choice (try-walkthrough.txt:1). How to tell it worked: extend devex-layout, or add a check, so that the inputSchema keys of each registerTool are compared with the table, and it passes.

qa/run.ts:124-125 and docs/QA-RUBRIC.md:94 (QA integrity and reproducibility). Only --only and --no-loop make a run dry, so 'npm run qa -- --skip build,ui-names' counts a loop. Skipped checks are 'left out' of automated = 1 + 9 × passed/total, so a counted loop can drop the checks that fail and still pass the gate. QA-RUBRIC lists this command as an ordinary one. Make --skip force a dry run, as --only does, or count skipped checks as failed in a counted loop. Change the docs example to 'npm run qa:dry -- --skip …'. How to tell it worked: 'npm run qa -- --skip engine-tests' leaves qa/state.json unchanged and prints 'not counted'.

No CI, and the QA checks read the working tree (the 'works on Windows and Unix' criterion). devex-crlf-tests and devex-gitattributes now catch the CRLF class of bug. My clone confirms they work. But Unix is never exercised, and the scratch copies are built from the working tree (QA-RUBRIC:104), so a file that is untracked or not committed can hide a broken HEAD. Add .github/workflows/ci.yml with 'npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build' on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest (no Playwright needed). Also have devex-crlf-tests copy 'git archive HEAD', or a 'git worktree add', instead of the working tree. How to tell it worked: a green badge for both OSes in the README, and a test that needs an untracked file fails the check.

A fresh 'npm ci' prints noise a contributor will ask about (setup honesty). The first warning is '1 moderate severity vulnerability': fflate 0.8.2, GHSA-px8p-9vwx-vf98. That advisory is about unzipSync. src/state.ts uses inflateSync and the build uses zipSync, so it cannot be reached, but bump fflate with 'npm audit fix' and commit the lockfile. The second is npm 11's 'allow-scripts … esbuild@0.28.2 (postinstall) not yet covered'. Approve it as the warning suggests (npm approve-scripts esbuild) and commit the result, or say in README:157 that it is harmless. Also, README:46 calls the GET /api/mcp?code= response 'a short info page', but it is raw JSON with beta.valid. Say 'a JSON info page: "valid": true'. How to tell it worked: npm ci on a fresh clone prints no warnings and 0 vulnerabilities.
